attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the safety-policy claim in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully isolates the safety-pledge assertion and correctly identifies Anthropic.

contract.note: Material weakening of the Responsible Scaling Policy is an ordinary reading of the statement. The February 24 revision falls clearly within the recent period preceding the post.

evidence.note: The preceding policy establishes the safeguards-dependent training restriction used as the comparison baseline. It does not independently establish the February revision.

Anthropic's dated announcement describes restructuring its safeguards framework around more limited unilateral commitments and nonbinding roadmap goals. This is primary evidence of its policy change, not an independent safety finding.
The revised policy retains conditional development pauses and procedural obligations. These limit the extent of the rollback but do not negate a material weakening of the central pledge.

reviews.rationale: The policy comparison supports a material weakening: the earlier safeguards-linked restriction gave way to nonbinding mitigation goals and narrower, competitor-dependent pause commitments. Retained safety obligations do not contradict this limited claim. The documents were published before the evaluation cutoff.
